Shares of BEML gained nearly in Friday’s trade after the state-owned engineering company secured an order worth more than Rs 5,400 crore from the National High Speed Rail Corporation Ltd (NHSRCL) for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor.
The stock rose as much as 5.36 per cent to Rs 2,121 on the BSE before paring some gains. The stock traded 2.73 higher at Rs 2,068 on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) in the afternoon session.
The contract covers the supply and maintenance of high-speed rolling stock, along with allied works, for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail (MAHSR) corridor, BEML said in an exchange filing.
The order comes as BEML builds its presence across the rail and metro segment while continuing to add contracts in defence, mining, construction and overseas markets.
BEML has secured several orders across its business verticals in recent weeks.
Earlier this month, the company received an order worth around Rs 180.6 crore from Integral Coach Factory for the manufacture and supply of Vande Bharat sleeper trainsets.
In August, BEML won a USD 6.65 million order from Mauritius for the phased supply of BE220G hydraulic excavators for deployment across African markets.
The company also secured a Rs 184.25 crore contract from Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd for the manufacture and supply of light combat helicopter fuselage aerostructures.

BEML operates across defence and aerospace, mining and construction, and rail and metro segments. In the June quarter, its consolidated revenue from operations rose 29.3 per cent year-on-year to Rs 819.62 crore, while its net loss narrowed to Rs 27.01 crore from Rs 64.11 crore a year earlier.

BEML chairman and managing director Shantanu Roy has said the company is targeting order inflows of around Rs 20,000 crore during the current financial year, subject to the finalisation of key tenders.
Roy has also indicated that BEML has potential orders worth more than Rs 40,000 crore across rail and metro, with additional opportunities emerging in mining, defence, construction and exports.

The latest NHSRCL contract adds to BEML’s high-speed rail portfolio. The company has previously said it is executing work related to the design, manufacture, supply, testing and commissioning of high-speed trainsets for the MAHSR corridor.

The size of the latest order also exceeds BEML’s consolidated FY26 revenue of around Rs 4,350 crore, although the contract covers both supply and maintenance and the company has not disclosed a revenue recognition schedule for the award.
